Tesla cancels 10-kW Powerwall, leaving only 7-kWh model

Thing is, 10kWh is the bare minimum that would be useful, and except for very small and efficient houses, it's really too small. A 5kW rooftop solar installation (and you wouldn't really go smaller these days) can generate 20-30 kWh on an average sunny day, and a family home can easily use 20kWh per day.

That said, they're quoting ~500 charge/discharge cycles for the Power Wall, which means it's essentially only going to last a couple of years at most. I'd say it's more likely that they pulled the product because it was terrible and needed to be re-engineered.

Edit: Apparently (as per the comments on that page) 500 was a typo and it's actually 5000 cycles, which is much better. In that case they probably realised that people were happily buying 7kWh versions, and that 3kWh of batteries for only $500 extra was losing money compared to people just doubling up on the 7kWh versions.

You don't install all this stuff and carry on burning energy like you did before. Energy saving appliances, timers on stuff that doesn't need to be on over night, insulate, get rid of inefficient heating and cooling systems. All of that means you can easily run a modern house on a lot less than 20kWh a day. That said, I don't think the powerwall is good value and intend to use my EV as a battery for my house because it has a much bigger battery than the powerwall does plus if my solar isn't generating enough to get by I can drive down to the local chargepoint and fill up to keep me going. Not planning to go off grid as yet because it is too expensive but I am generating more power than I use and I still have to get full insulation and double glazing in.
